title: filter p over join — the tuning fork among the List strings
transcribed_from: pdftocairo -svg page 61, the paths inside the bboxes below; one 400dpi crop at -x 620 -y 930 -W 1060 -H 480
note: The page prints `filter p ⋅ join A = join A ⋅ List (filter p)`; the component `A` is dropped, as it is for `η A` on p. 74, and the application is bracketed because juxtaposition here is composition and nothing else. `join : List∘List →̇ List` is the tuning fork the text names (p. 46), and on the page the object wire slides past its dot — the naturality licence p. 40 §2.2.4 states, and the whole of the declared `spider-vs-bead`: the spider bends that wire in instead, so `A` is join's last arm and a leg of its own, which is the weaker claim the type `List(List(A)) → List(A)` itself makes. `filter p` is the other case: the page says it is `an arrow of type List A → List A` `attached to the strings`, and an arrow is a transformation between CONSTANT functors, so its dot sits on the object wire — it breaks BOTH strings, the `List` wire bending into it and a new one out. Interior segments carry no label in the book.

sigs.//: The book's own letters for THIS equation. `filter` is keyed by its head, so the bead is drawn `filter(p)` and typed by the row `filter`; its source and target are objects, not schemes, which is what puts it on the object wire.
